claims.text: FortKnox supports Azure Private Endpoint connectivity for its cloud vaults
FortKnox vaults reachable via Azure Private Endpoint through ExpressRoute or Azure VPN
FortKnox can deploy and configure Azure Private Endpoints to protect all backup and recovery traffic
Cohesity cluster provides a secure private data path via ExpressRoute or Azure VPN through a Private Endpoint [1]
Recovery Services vault private endpoints use a VNet IP and Microsoft backbone private link, eliminating public internet exposure
Azure Backup creates private endpoints for the storage accounts, keeping backup traffic in the VNet
With a vault private endpoint, ExpressRoute Private Peering is required for on-prem backup traffic
On-premises network must be peered with the VNet holding the vault's private endpoint
Contrast: FortKnox via PE over ER/VPN vs Azure requiring ER Private Peering

A.notes: [1] is the subnet-configuration step and never mentions ExpressRoute/VPN. Missing resource-ID request, per-region endpoint, and new-vault-only/MABS v4 restriction.

claims.text: FortKnox vaults reachable via Azure Private Endpoint through ExpressRoute or Azure VPN
Private Endpoint is a NIC using a private VNet IP, bringing the service into the VNet
FortKnox can deploy Private Endpoints to protect all backup and recovery traffic
Setup: request storage-account resource ID from Cohesity by email, subnet config, deployment, approval, host mapping; unique resource ID per region; vault set up first
RSV private endpoints use private VNet IPs
Private endpoint tied to a NIC; DNS mapping redirects service/blob/queue traffic
Extensions try the private URL then fall back to the public URL
Microsoft recommends public network access Deny; set under vault > Networking > Public access
Deny without private endpoint: backups succeed, restores fail except VMs, VM item-level recovery fails
DNS options; 'Integrate with private DNS zone' creates entries automatically
Service creates private endpoints for storage accounts; vault needs permissions for PEs and DNS zones
ExpressRoute Private Peering required for on-prem traffic with a vault PE; MABS v4 or later
PEs used for SQL/SAP HANA in VMs, MARS, DPM/MABS, and VM file recovery
Entra ID has no private endpoint; allow its IPs/FQDNs outbound (NSG/Firewall tags)
~11 private IPs (v1) or up to 10+n (MABS); PEs only for new vaults with no registered items

B.notes: All claims supported; misses that each Azure region needs its own private endpoint (shared across clusters).

claims.text: AWS Backup copies to other Regions on demand or automatically in a scheduled backup plan
Cross-Region replication is valuable for business continuity/compliance distance requirements
First copy to a new Region is full; later copies generally incremental if supported
Copy re-encrypted with destination vault's customer managed key; EBS different key forces full copy, same key stays incremental
Console steps: create plan, add rule, Copy to destination with Region and vault, one copy rule per destination
Do not toggle 'Copy to another account's vault' for cross-Region copies
Most resources and most Regions support cross-Region backup
No cross-Region copies for cold-tier storage
If a resource type lacks cross-Region copy, no copy in any scenario incl. same-Region different vault
Cross-Region copy of a continuous backup becomes a snapshot backup; no PITR
No SLAs for copy job completion times

A.notes: Accurate and fully supported; omits the RDS option-group requirement.

claims.text: Cross-Region copy jobs are encrypted with the target vault's KMS key
A copy to another Region is encrypted with the destination vault's key
Cross-Region backup copies to a destination Region and most Regions support it [6]
AWS Backup lets you choose the destination Region for the copy [5]
Cross-Region copy requires updating a backup plan to change the copy Region
All tags of the original backup are copied to the destination Region
Cross-Region copy supported for continuous backups when the resource type supports it
Cross-Region copy of S3 backups supported in opt-in Regions
Continuous backups (transaction logs) cannot be copied to other Regions or accounts
Option groups cannot be copied; create the same option group in the destination Region first

B.notes: [5] is a cross-account vault-access page; [6] shows the Copy to destination step but not that most Regions support it. Misses on-demand vs copy-rule mechanics, full-then-incremental, and cold-tier limit; the transaction-log statement is SAP HANA-specific and contradicts its own [9] claim.
